K2 Space , a Torrance, California-based developer of large, high-powered satellites, also picked up a big round, securing $500 million in Series D funding in July. For a broader view, below we put together a list of nine of this year’s largest space tech funding round recipients. Exits rising Needless to say, space tech investors aren’t just deploying capital — they’re also seeing eye-popping exit returns. SpaceX set an initial valuation of nearly $1.8 trillion for its June IPO — the largest by far of any public offering to date — and raised over $80 billion in the process. Shares of the rocket developer, launch provider, Starlink operator and AI hyperscaler have fluctuated since then, but recently hovered near the initial offer price. Of course, no other company operating in the space tech sector will come close to that. Leaving that aside, however, we did see some offerings and acquisitions that were significant by most other comps. One example was York Space Systems , a private equity-backed space and defense tech company, which went public in January at a valuation of over $4 billion. Its stock has fallen sharply since then, however, indicating that a space tech focus alone is not enough to keep shares aloft. More recently, HawkEye 360 , operator of a satellite constellation that sells signals intelligence to defense and government customers, went public in May. Its shares are also down some from their first-day closing price. Startup M&A deals are also happening. York Space Systems announced this year that it is acquiring All.Space , a provider of satellite communications terminals, in a $355 million deal. It acquired two other venture-backed companies this year for undisclosed sums: Orbion Space Technology , a developer of satellite propulsion systems, and Solestial , focused on solar energy for space. Another recent market entrant, Voyager Technologies , also made a significant acquisition, picking up Astrobotic Technology , a developer of lunar landers and rovers, for $300 million in June. Risks and rewards Of course, even the most sunnily optimistic startup investors don’t expect space tech valuations to always move up and to the right. It’s a notoriously risk-prone sector, and even the sector’s high-valuation market newcomer, SpaceX, has suffered its share of rocket failures and other high-profile disappointments. That said, startup backers clearly believe space tech rewards outweigh the risks. We’ll see in coming quarters if that still holds true. You'll join the Tribe building for managers, the people who plan work, protect margins, and keep projects on time and on budget.</p> <p>You own significant parts of that experience end-to-end, working hands-on with product and design to ship work that matters. You'll do this as we build and launch Toggl 2.0, our consolidated planning, time tracking, and time intelligence product.</p> <p>The salary for this position is&nbsp;<strong>€83,000 annually.</strong></p> <p>You can work from anywhere in the world&nbsp;<strong>as long as your main location is between UTC-4 and UTC+4.</strong></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>The Role</strong></h2> <p>As a Senior Full Stack Engineer, you own meaningful parts of the product end-to-end, from the data model and the API to the interface someone actually clicks: the technical approach, the quality of what ships, and whether it actually works for the people using it. You are accountable not for tickets closed, but for clarity, craft, and outcomes.</p> <p>You'll work in the Tribe serving managers, across planning and capacity management, dashboards, and billable work. This is some of the most data-dense, interaction-heavy surface area in the product: schedules and capacity views, reports, and visualizations that have to stay fast and readable at real customer scale. The interesting problems live on both sides of the API here - the query behind a capacity view matters as much as how that view renders. You'll build with React and TypeScript on the frontend and our backend services (mostly Golang) and data layer (Postgres) behind them, alongside a product manager, a designer, and engineers who are used to owning their work and pushing back when something isn't right. In a tribe of 5 other engineers, your impact and visibility are high.</p> <p>Our team meetings are scheduled between 11:00 and 16:00 UTC. Your availability and commitment to participate in these sessions are essential for effective collaboration and team alignment.</p> <p>Your main responsibilities will be:</p> <p><strong>Ownership and delivery</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Take projects from problem to production. Own the technical approach for major features front to back, break the work down sensibly, sequence it, and ship in slices rather than one big drop.</p> </li> <li> <p>Make the technical calls in your area. Choose between options, name the tradeoffs, and decide without waiting for permission or escalating routine judgment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Keep your work visible without being chased. Flag risks and slips early, keep the Tribe in the loop, and unblock yourself.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Craft and quality across the stack</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Build interfaces people trust with dense, real-world data. Planning views, dashboards, and reports that stay fast, accessible, and readable when the dataset gets ugly.</p> </li> <li> <p>Design the data and API layer those views depend on. Model it so the feature you're building now doesn't make the next three harder.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own performance as a feature, end to end. Profile, measure, and fix the slow query and the slow render instead of hoping the data stays small.</p> </li> <li> <p>Write code others can work in. Sensible components and services, real test coverage where it earns its keep, and a codebase that's easier to change after you touch it.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Working with product and design</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Shape solutions, don't just implement them. Push on the problem, question requirements that don't hold up, and propose simpler paths when you see one.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner closely with design. Prototype early, spot the edge cases in a flow before it's built, and hold the bar on UX quality with your designer rather than after handoff.</p> </li> <li> <p>Stay close to users and evidence. Join user tests, read the feedback, look at the data, and let it change what you build.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Raising the bar</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Review code with intent. Give precise, actionable feedback that makes the change and the person better.</p> </li> <li> <p>Mentor and interview. Help other engineers grow, and help us hire well.</p> </li> <li> <p>Improve things across team boundaries. Spot shared components and duplicated work between Tribes, and raise it before we build the same thing twice.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>AI as core leverage</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Use AI tools extensively in your daily work for exploration, prototyping, code generation and review, debugging, research, and writing. AI fluency is not optional. It's part of how you increase your speed, depth, and impact - and you're expected to help the rest of the Tribe get better at it too.</p> </li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>About You</strong></h2> <p>You will thrive in this role if you:</p> <ul> <li> <p>Have significant experience building and shipping production web applications end to end, and can lead major projects rather than just contribute to them.</p> </li> <li> <p>Are genuinely comfortable on both sides of the stack. You're deep on one side and properly capable on the other, not someone who hands off at the API boundary.</p> </li> <li> <p>Have deep, practical knowledge of&nbsp;<strong>JavaScript, TypeScript, React, and modern CSS</strong>&nbsp;- including state management and side-effect handling in large applications.</p> </li> <li> <p>Are solid on backend fundamentals: at least one backend language you know well, API design, relational data modelling, and enough instinct for query performance to spot the problem before production does.&nbsp;<strong>Prior Golang experience is not mandatory but you have to be willing to adopt it and become comfortable with it fast.</strong></p> </li> <li> <p>Hold an extremely high bar for quality. You know what great looks like, you notice the details others miss, and you don't ship work you wouldn't put your name on.</p> </li> <li> <p>Have a knack for data-heavy product surfaces - performance, readability, and the principles behind a chart that actually communicates something.</p> </li> <li> <p>Care about the user's problem, not just the ticket. newContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Animalz: Senior Content Marketer, SEO Anywhere in the World New York Content Writing, Content Creation, SEO, On-Page SEO, SEO Writing, and Content Planning Sales and Marketing Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0017/3233/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> San Diego, California <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://animalz.co">https://animalz.co</a> </p> <p>We're looking for a Senior Content Marketer: an exceptional writer with the editorial judgment to own content quality for the customers they serve.</p> <p>This is a writing-first role. About 70% of your time will be spent researching and writing content yourself—work that calls for real research, original thinking, and craft.</p> <p>On the SEO team, that writing is built to perform in search: blog posts, guides, and landing pages that satisfy search intent and still read like something a person wanted to write. Search itself is changing, and this role sits right in the middle of that change. Alongside traditional rankings, you'll help customer content get found and cited by AI search tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's AI Overviews.</p> <p>The rest of your time goes to making sure everything else your accounts publish is just as good as what you write. You'll manage the freelance writers who contribute to your accounts, keep the content calendar on track, review every piece before it reaches the customer, and ensure customer feedback is acted on and remembered.</p> <p>You won't do any of this alone. Every account is served by a small team, and you'll work alongside teammates who own the overall strategy and the customer relationship. Your ownership is the content itself: writing much of it, and standing behind all of it.</p> <h2>What You'll Do</h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>Write high-quality content designed to rank</strong>, weaving keyword research, search intent, and on-page best practices into genuinely good writing, grounded in a real understanding of each customer's product and audience</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Review every piece your accounts deliver</strong> before it reaches the customer, whether you wrote it, a freelancer wrote it, or it started as an AI-assisted draft. (Note: we have separate Editors who edit pieces in production for feedback. Your role is the final review)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Refresh and optimize existing content to improve rankings</strong>, engagement, and visibility, in both traditional search and AI-powered discovery</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Diagnose why a piece isn't performing</strong>, using tools like GA4, Google Search Console, and Ahrefs, and recommend clear, prioritized improvements</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Help manage the freelance writers on your accounts</strong>, write briefs they can succeed with, and maintain customer brand guides and other assets for reference.</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Act on customer feedback quickly and thoroughly</strong>, and keep track of it, so a customer never has to give the same note twice</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Communicate directly with customers about deliverables</strong>, timelines, and revisions, and join customer calls as a trusted voice on the work</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Help improve our AI-assisted content workflows</strong> by using them on real work and feeding back what you learn</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Contribute to performance reporting</strong>, helping show customers what shipped, how it's performing, and what we're learning</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Use AI tools thoughtfully,</strong> taking advantage of them where they genuinely help, and applying your own judgment and craft where they don't</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Contribute to team knowledge-sharing and internal initiatives</strong>, learning from teammates and sharing what you know</p> </li> </ul> <h2>What We're Looking For</h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>4–6 years of experience in content marketing</strong>, with at least 2 of those years in B2B SaaS.
